key_insight: EDEN boosts RLVR exploration by perturbing the input embedding at rollout time, creating more diverse trajectories without changing the model architecture or inference pipeline.
engineering_relevance: It offers a lightweight, training-time-only way to improve mathematical reasoning coverage and strengthen group-relative learning signals under the same rollout budget.
method: Adds a single perturbed embedding position to some prompts as an anchored source of directional noise.
Uses Gaussian noise plus a shared anchor to keep perturbations diverse yet group-consistent.
Mixes selected perturbed rollouts into GRPO with downweighted advantages; decoding and test-time inference stay unchanged.
evidence_signal: Across multiple model scales and math-reasoning benchmarks, EDEN outperformed GRPO and other exploration controls, with the biggest gains in sampled solution coverage and more groups receiving non-zero learning signals.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful tuning of noise level, anchor design, and the fraction of perturbed rollouts to avoid destabilizing training or weakening useful advantage signals.
paper_title: Beyond Policy Rollouts: Embedding-Space Directional Exploration with Anchored Noise for LLM RLVR
